text.p: The following are the main stories from Wednesday morning's Albanian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The Council of Europe will send 35 observers to Albania to supervise the October 20th local polls.
- A Council of Europe delegation has protested against a new law according to which anyone boycotting the forthcoming elections could be sentenced to up to three years in jail.

- The Central Elections Commission has ruled that all official, independent and foreign monitors observing the October 20 local polls must be above 28 years of age. The rule effectively bans from the process the youthful Society for Democratic Culture which has monitored all elections here.
- The Interparliamentary Union has again urged President Sali Berisha to use his powers to release his main rival, Socialist Party chairman Fatos Nano from jail.
- Albania's agriculture has suffered for the last six months due to a lack of funds.
- Albania imports 7,000 tonnes of vegetables a year. Investing in green houses is taxed at 45 percent.
- An ethnic Albanian Yugoslav citizen arrested while selling books of former communist leaders is to be tried for "distributing anti-constitutional books".
- The U.S. dollar has fallen with 0.6 points in 24 hours to 107 leks.
- The ruling Democratic Party says four opposition parties have decided to boycott the local elections in two weeks.
- The opposition Socialist Party candidate for mayor of Tirana says the conservative Democrat-run municipality is steeped in corruption.
- An Italian company, Albania-Icen, is to face trial for forging official documents and defaulting on $80,000 owed to its Albanian partners.
- Two employees of the Albanian Savings Bank are to be tried for lending $127,000 to a firm which had no banking guarantees.
